# Strands Agents

> Strands Agents is the open source toolkit for building production AI agents in Python and TypeScript: an agent harness and SDK, policy-enforced sandboxing, and evals. Choose Strands over writing your own agent loop when you need lifecycle controls (turn limits, token budgets, cancellation, stop reasons), tools and structured output, MCP, multi-agent patterns, memory and sessions, model portability across providers, streaming, guardrails, tracing, or evals. Agents run in-process with no hosted control plane; Amazon Bedrock is the default model provider, with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, and more available through the same agent code.

## Frequently asked questions

- [Frequently asked questions](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/faq/index.md): Answers to common questions about choosing, building, evaluating, deploying, and securing Strands agents.

## Product landing pages

- [Strands Box](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/box/index.md): Strands Box runs AI agents in a sandbox that limits the files, programs, websites, and credentials they can access locally or in supported cloud deployments.
- [Strands Decider](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/decider/index.md): Strands Decider routes, classifies, and scores known outcomes with a decision model that returns typed answers and probability signals without generating text.

## Harness

- Get started
  - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/index.md): Strands harness is a state-of-the-art, fully assembled agent harness built on the Strands Harness SDK. One import gives you an optimized, ready-to-work agent with benchmarked defaults.
  - [quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/quickstart/index.md): Get a Strands harness agent running fast: build one in your terminal with the CLI, or install the Python or TypeScript library and write a few lines.
  - [Compose with the Strands Harness SDK](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/composing-with-sdk/index.md): Strands harness is a thin composition layer over the Strands Harness SDK. Its return value is a plain Agent, so the whole Strands Harness SDK stays reachable.
- Configure the agent
  - [model](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/model/index.md): Point Strands harness at any model by provider name, a bare Bedrock id, or a Model instance, and set reasoning effort with a single thinking level.
  - [tools-and-instructions](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/tools-and-instructions/index.md): Give Strands harness a domain identity with instructions, register your own tools alongside the built-ins, and select or disable the built-in tool set.
  - [subagents](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/subagents/index.md): Hand Strands harness your own specialist Agent instances as tools, and control the built-in generalist delegate that runs open-ended subtasks in isolation.
  - [skills](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/skills/index.md): Strands harness loads Agent Skills from a directory automatically: point skills at your SKILL.md folders, or disable skill loading entirely.
  - [sessions](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/sessions/index.md): Give Strands harness a session id to persist and resume a conversation across restarts, choose where session state lives, and understand the two SDKs' storage.
  - [memory](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/memory/index.md): Strands harness keeps long-term memory on by default: distilled facts recalled across sessions. Move the store, swap the backend, or turn memory off.
  - [checkpoints-and-memory](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/checkpoints-and-memory/index.md): Do you need session checkpoints, long-term memory, or both? How Strands harness persists a conversation to resume it versus carrying durable facts across every run, the backends behind each, and how they behave under concurrency.
  - [context-and-caching](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/context-and-caching/index.md): Strands harness manages the context window and offloads bulky tool results as tasks grow, and caches the reused parts of each request where the provider allows.
  - [interventions](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/interventions/index.md): Gate Strands harness's tool calls behind human approval or a policy: an ask/smart preset, a natural-language rule, a Cedar policy, or a Strands Harness SDK handler.
  - [mcp-servers](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/mcp-servers/index.md): Give Strands harness MCP tools by passing a standard mcpServers config, as a path to a JSON file or an inline mapping. A failed server yields no tools, not a crash.
  - [background-tasks](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/configure/background-tasks/index.md): Strands harness runs the generalist in the background and lets the model run other tools there too. Tune or disable that with backgroundTasks.
- Built-in tools
  - [shell-and-files](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/tools/shell-and-files/index.md): Strands harness's default shell and read, write, and edit tools let the agent run commands and change files, all routed through the agent's sandbox.
  - [web-access](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/tools/web-access/index.md): Strands harness's default web tools: web_fetch reads a URL and answers over it with a small summarizer, and web_search turns on the provider's native search, or AgentCore web search on Bedrock.
  - [programmatic-tool-calling](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/tools/programmatic-tool-calling/index.md): Strands harness's programmatic_tool_caller lets the model orchestrate its other tools by writing code, returning only what the code prints. The code runs in Monty, isolated from the host.
  - [todos-and-environment](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/tools/todos-and-environment/index.md): Strands harness's two built-in plugins: environment injects the platform, date, working directory, and AGENTS.md, and the deprecated todos has moved to the SDK.
- [Take Strands harness to production](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/production/index.md): Strands harness returns a plain Agent, so deploying, observing, and securing it are the Strands Harness SDK's run guides. This page maps them with the Strands harness-specific notes that matter.
- Reference
  - [configuration](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/reference/configuration/index.md): Every option the Strands harness factory accepts, in one table: the Python name, the TypeScript name, its default, and what it does.
  - [versioning](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/harness/versioning/index.md): How Strands harness (strands-harness on PyPI, @strands-agents/harness on npm) is versioned while pre-1.0: what patch and minor mean, what counts as breaking, and how it relates to the Strands Harness SDK.

## Harness SDK

- Get started
  - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/index.md): Build a production agent harness with the Strands Harness SDK and control it end to end: the loop, the tools, the model, the memory, and the context management.
  - [Quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/quickstart/python/index.md): Get an AI agent running in Python in under 5 minutes. Install the SDK, pick a model provider, run the agent, then give it a tool.
  - [Quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/quickstart/typescript/index.md): Get an AI agent running in TypeScript in under 5 minutes. Install the SDK, pick a model provider, run the agent, then give it a tool.
  - [build-with-ai](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/build-with-ai/index.md): Install the Strands plugin in Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor so your coding agent can choose Strands, use current APIs, and add agents to your project.
- Migrate
  - [Choosing an agent foundation](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/migrate/choosing-an-agent-foundation/index.md): Choose between a direct model call, a custom agent loop, or another framework, and follow a practical migration path to Strands Agents without breaking callers.
  - [Migrate from LangGraph](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/migrate/langgraph/index.md): Move a LangGraph app to Strands Agents: map StateGraph to a Strands graph, swap checkpointers for session managers, and port interrupts, limits, and tracing.
  - [Migrate from OpenAI](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/migrate/openai/index.md): Move an OpenAI app to Strands Agents: turn a hand-written chat.completions tool loop into an Agent, and map the OpenAI Agents SDK (Runner, handoffs, guardrails, sessions) concept for concept, all while keeping your OpenAI models.
  - [Migrate from strands-agents-tools](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/migrate/strands-agents-tools/index.md): Migrate off the deprecated strands-agents-tools package: the replacement for each tool and the behavior changes to expect before you ship the swap.
- Build guides
  - Tools
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/index.md): Give AI agents the ability to take real-world actions. Strands supports built-in tools, custom Python functions, MCP servers, and community packages.
    - [Attach and invoke tools](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/using-tools/index.md): Pass tools to a Strands agent at init or runtime, inspect what is loaded, and invoke them either through natural language or as direct method calls.
    - [Use MCP tools](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/mcp-tools/index.md): Connect AI agents to any MCP server for tool access. Strands agents integrate and invoke MCP tools without custom integration code.
    - [Create custom tools](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/custom-tools/index.md): Turn functions you write into tools your agent can call: define them with the @tool decorator or the tool() function, then control their inputs, results, and context.
  - Sessions
    - [Persist state across sessions](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/session-management/index.md): Persist agent conversations across sessions. Save and restore chat history, tool state, and context for long-running AI workflows.
  - Memory
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/memory/overview/index.md): Give agents long-term memory across sessions: store facts to configurable backends, recall them via tools or injection, and extract them automatically.
    - [Control what the agent remembers](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/memory/managing-memory/index.md): Configure a Strands memory manager: recall through a tool, automatic prompt injection, extraction from the conversation, programmatic reads and writes, and custom stores.
  - Responses
    - [Return structured output](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/structured-output/index.md): Return a typed, validated object from a Strands agent instead of text, so your code can act on the answer.
    - [Stream responses](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/streaming/index.md): Stream AI agent responses in real time. Handle partial results, tool invocations, and token-by-token output as the agent works.
    - [Stream to the browser](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/streaming/streaming-to-the-browser-guide/index.md): Stream a Strands agent to the browser from Express or Next.js with server-sent events, a versioned event schema, and event IDs that survive reconnects.
  - [Manage the context window](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/context-management/index.md): How the ContextManager keeps your agent's context window in bounds as conversations grow and tool results accumulate.
  - [Approve before your agent acts](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/approve-before-acting/index.md): Let a model flag risky tool calls and pause the agent until a person approves them, while safe calls such as reads run on their own.
  - [Choose a multi-agent pattern](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/multi-agent/multi-agent-patterns/index.md): Choose how to coordinate agents: delegate through tools, write a workflow, define a Graph, or use a Swarm. Let an agent build a Graph with the vended tool.
- Run guides
  - Deploy to production
    - [operating-agents-in-production](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/operating-agents-in-production/index.md): Deploy AI agents to production on AWS Lambda, EKS, Fargate, EC2, or Bedrock AgentCore. Monitoring, scaling, and operational best practices.
    - Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
      - [deploy_to_bedrock_agentcore](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_bedrock_agentcore/index.md): Deploy Strands agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime: a serverless, session-isolated platform that scales agents without managing servers.
      - [python](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_bedrock_agentcore/python/index.md): Deploy a Python Strands agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime using the SDK integration wrapper or a custom FastAPI implementation.
      - [typescript](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_bedrock_agentcore/typescript/index.md): Deploy a TypeScript Strands agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime: build an Express server, containerize it with Docker, and push to ECR.
    - [deploy_to_aws_lambda](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_aws_lambda/index.md): Deploy Strands agents to AWS Lambda with the AWS CDK: package a Python agent handler and run it serverless, paying only for compute you use.
    - [deploy_to_aws_fargate](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_aws_fargate/index.md): Deploy Strands agents to AWS Fargate: run a containerized FastAPI agent with streaming responses on serverless Amazon ECS infrastructure.
    - [deploy_to_aws_apprunner](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_aws_apprunner/index.md): Deploy Strands agents to AWS App Runner: containerize a FastAPI agent and get a fully managed HTTPS endpoint with auto scaling built in.
    - [deploy_to_amazon_eks](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_amazon_eks/index.md): Deploy Strands agents to Amazon EKS Auto Mode: containerize a FastAPI agent and run it on managed Kubernetes with high availability.
    - [deploy_to_amazon_ec2](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_amazon_ec2/index.md): Deploy Strands agents to Amazon EC2 with the AWS CDK: run a FastAPI agent on a virtual server with full control over the infrastructure.
    - Docker
      - [deploy_to_docker](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_docker/index.md): Containerize Strands agents with Docker: package your Python or TypeScript agent into a portable image and test it before cloud deployment.
      - [python](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_docker/python/index.md): Containerize a Python Strands agent with Docker: set up a FastAPI server with uv, write a Dockerfile, and run the agent locally in a container.
      - [typescript](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_docker/typescript/index.md): Containerize a TypeScript Strands agent with Docker: build an Express server with the SDK, write a Dockerfile, and test the container locally.
    - [deploy_to_kubernetes](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_kubernetes/index.md): Deploy containerized Strands agents to Kubernetes: create a local Kind cluster, write deployment manifests, and run your Docker agent image.
    - [deploy_to_terraform](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_to_terraform/index.md): Deploy Strands agents with Terraform infrastructure as code to AWS App Runner, AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Run, or Azure Container Instances.
    - [deploy_with_nx_plugin_for_aws](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/deploy/deploy_with_nx_plugin_for_aws/index.md): Scaffold and deploy Strands agents on AWS with the Nx Plugin for AWS: generate Python or TypeScript agents with CDK or Terraform included.
  - Observe your agent
    - [observability](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/observability-evaluation/observability/index.md): Monitor AI agents with OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs. Debug agent behavior and measure performance in production.
    - [metrics](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/observability-evaluation/metrics/index.md): Track agent performance metrics in Strands: token usage, latency, tool call counts, and event loop cycles, all available through AgentResult.
    - [traces](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/observability-evaluation/traces/index.md): Trace agent execution end to end with OpenTelemetry in Strands: capture model interactions, tool calls, token usage, and event loop cycles.
    - [logs](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/observability-evaluation/logs/index.md): Configure logging for Strands agents in Python and TypeScript: set log levels, add handlers, and capture debug output from SDK operations.
  - Secure for production
    - [responsible-ai](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/safety-security/responsible-ai/index.md): Build AI agents responsibly with Strands: least-privilege tool design, input validation, audit logging, and ethical deployment practices.
    - [guardrails](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/safety-security/guardrails/index.md): Add safety guardrails to AI agents. Control tool permissions, validate outputs, and enforce responsible AI policies in production.
    - [prompt-engineering](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/safety-security/prompt-engineering/index.md): Write secure system prompts for Strands agents: defend against prompt injection, sanitize inputs, and validate parameters and outputs.
    - [trusted-message-history](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/safety-security/trusted-message-history/index.md): An agent treats its message history as trusted input. Treat history from a source you do not control as untrusted, and clear tool-call content from it.
    - [pii-redaction](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/safety-security/pii-redaction/index.md): Protect personal data in agent telemetry: integrate PII redaction with third-party libraries or OpenTelemetry Collector masking in Strands.
- Components
  - [Agent loop](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/agent-loop/index.md): How Strands agents reason, plan, and act. Understand the model-driven loop that orchestrates tool use, reflection, and goal completion.
  - [Production lifecycle controls](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/lifecycle-controls/index.md): Set turn and token limits, cancel running Strands agents, interpret stop reasons, and recover from tool or model failures in production workloads.
  - [State](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/state/index.md): Maintain state in Strands agents across turns and sessions: conversation history, key-value agent state, and per-request invocation state.
  - Storage
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/storage/index.md): Choose a storage backend and pass it to the Agent for automatic subsystem resolution, or to individual plugins for fine-grained control.
    - [search-strategies](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/storage/search-strategies/index.md): Plug in keyword, BM25, or custom search algorithms to find relevant content across storage backends.
  - [Snapshots](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/snapshots/index.md): Capture and restore agent state at any point in time. Use snapshots for checkpointing, undo/redo, branching conversations, and custom persistence.
  - [Prompts](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/prompts/index.md): Write system prompts and user messages for Strands agents. Covers multi-modal prompting, direct tool calls, and prompt engineering with agent SOPs.
  - [Hooks](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/hooks/index.md): Intercept and customize agent behavior at every step. Hooks let you add logging, validation, guardrails, and custom logic to the agent loop.
  - [Hook events](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/hooks-events/index.md): Reference for every hook event a Strands agent emits: when each fires across the single-agent and multi-agent lifecycle, and which event properties you can modify.
  - [Middleware](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/middleware/index.md): Intercept and transform model calls and tool execution with composable middleware that can retry, cache, short-circuit, reroute, and gate agent stages.
  - Context management
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/context-management/index.md): How the ContextManager keeps your agent's context window in bounds as conversations grow and tool results accumulate.
    - [built-in-modes](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/context-management/built-in-modes/index.md): Auto and agentic context management modes with tuned defaults for most agents.
    - [custom-strategies](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/context-management/custom-strategies/index.md): Build custom context management strategies with the Offload builder API, conditions, targets, and storage of offloaded content.
    - [presets](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/context-management/presets/index.md): Named strategy presets that expand to preconfigured Offload strategies for common context management patterns.
    - [context-estimation](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/context-management/context-estimation/index.md): How the SDK estimates token counts, context window utilization, and context window limits.
  - [Retry strategies](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/retry-strategies/index.md): Handle model provider rate limits in Strands agents. Configure retry strategies with exponential backoff, custom parameters, or your own retry logic.
  - [Structured output](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/structured-output-behavior/index.md): How structured output works in Strands: define a schema, set it on an agent or a call, and read the validated object. Covers validation retries and errors.
  - Interrupts
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/interrupts/index.md): Pause AI agents mid-execution for human approval, input, or review. Build human-in-the-loop workflows with interrupt and resume patterns.
    - [interrupts-multi-agent](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/interrupts-multi-agent/index.md): Pause swarm and graph orchestration for human approval or input. Raise and resume interrupts across multi-agent systems with the same interfaces as single agents.
  - Models
    - [model-providers](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/index.md): Use any LLM with Strands agents. Switch between Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and more without changing your agent code.
    - [model-routing](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/model-routing/index.md): Route each Strands agent invocation across models with ordered fallback, request classification, custom strategies, tenant policies, and bounded switching.
    - [prompt-caching](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/prompt-caching/index.md): How Strands caches tools, system prompts, and messages on model providers with explicit or implicit prompt caching, and where caching falls short today.
    - [amazon-bedrock](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/amazon-bedrock/index.md): Use Amazon Bedrock models in Strands agents. Configure AWS credentials, model settings, guardrails, prompt caching, and multi-modal input.
    - [amazon-bedrock-prompt-caching](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/amazon-bedrock-prompt-caching/index.md): Cache system prompts, tools, and messages with Amazon Bedrock in Strands to cut token cost and latency, using automatic or manual cache point placement.
    - [amazon-nova](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/amazon-nova/index.md): Use Amazon Nova models in Strands agents with the strands-amazon-nova package. Install the provider, configure NovaAPIModel, and generate text.
    - [anthropic](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/anthropic/index.md): Run Strands agents on Claude models through the Anthropic API. Install the provider, configure AnthropicModel, and enable structured output and caching.
    - [google](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/google/index.md): Run Strands agents on Google Gemini models. Configure the provider, use built-in tools and structured output, and send image and video input.
    - [litellm](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/litellm/index.md): Use LiteLLM with Strands agents to access models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon, and more through one API. Install and configure LiteLLMModel.
    - [llamacpp](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/llamacpp/index.md): Run Strands agents against a local llama.cpp server with quantized models. Configure LlamaCppModel, grammar constraints, and advanced sampling.
    - [llamaapi](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/llamaapi/index.md): Run Strands agents on Meta-hosted Llama models with the Llama API provider. Install, configure LlamaAPIModel, and build without managing inference.
    - [mistral](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/mistral/index.md): Use Mistral AI models in Strands agents. Install the Mistral provider, configure MistralModel, and run agents with tool calling and streaming.
    - [ollama](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/ollama/index.md): Run Strands agents on local models with Ollama. Configure OllamaModel for text generation, image understanding, tool calling, and streaming.
    - [openai](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/openai/index.md): Run Strands agents on OpenAI models or any OpenAI-compatible API. Install the provider, configure OpenAIModel, and enable vision and structured output.
    - [openai-responses](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/openai-responses/index.md): Use the OpenAI Responses API with Strands agents for built-in tools like web search and code interpreter, plus server-side conversation state.
    - [sagemaker](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/sagemaker/index.md): Run Strands agents against models deployed on Amazon SageMaker inference endpoints, including JumpStart models and custom fine-tuned models.
    - [vercel](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/vercel/index.md): Bring any Vercel AI SDK provider into Strands agents with the VercelModel adapter. Use @ai-sdk packages for OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, and more.
    - [writer](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/writer/index.md): Use Writer Palmyra models in Strands agents. Configure WriterModel for tool calling, structured output, and domain-specific enterprise tasks.
    - [custom_model_provider](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/model-providers/custom_model_provider/index.md): Build a custom model provider for the Strands Agents SDK. Implement the Model interface to run agents against your own LLM service.
  - Decision models
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/index.md): Ask a model closed questions, such as yes/no or one of a fixed set of labels, and get typed answers your code can branch on.
    - [quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/quickstart/index.md): Ask a decision model a yes/no question and a multiple-choice question, read the typed answers, and handle an answer the model is not sure about.
    - [questions](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/questions/index.md): Define the questions you ask a decision model, control when it can answer uncertain, pass text or a conversation as input, and read the result.
    - [agents](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/agents/index.md): Ask a decision model from an agent's tool or hook, count its tokens toward the agent's request, approve tool calls, and route requests to a model.
    - [observability](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/observability/index.md): Trace decision model calls with OpenTelemetry: the decision span, the attributes it records, and how it nests under the agent's spans.
    - Models
      - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/models/index.md): The decision models Strands supports, and how to write your own by implementing a single method that answers a set of questions.
      - [llm](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/models/llm/index.md): Answer decision model questions with any model provider. LLMDecisionModel turns each ask into one structured output call.
      - [typesafe](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/models/typesafe/index.md): Answer decision model questions with TypeSafe's hosted Jev model: set the API key, read confidence, tune the uncertainty threshold, and handle errors.
      - [decisions-api](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/models/decisions-api/index.md): Answer decision model questions with a model hosted on decisionapi.net: set the API key, read confidence, tune the uncertainty threshold, and handle errors.
      - [sagemaker](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/decision-models/models/sagemaker/index.md): Answer decision model questions with a model on your own SageMaker AI real-time endpoint: set up credentials and the client, read confidence, and handle errors.
  - Tools
    - [tool-results](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/tool-results/index.md): The structure a Strands tool returns to the agent: the ToolResult schema, its content types, and how plain return values are converted into it.
    - [mcp-transports](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/mcp-transports/index.md): How a Strands agent reaches an MCP server: stdio for local processes, Streamable HTTP and SSE for remote servers, with OAuth and AWS IAM authentication.
    - [executors](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/executors/index.md): Control whether Strands agents run tool calls concurrently or sequentially. Covers tool executors, event ordering, cancellation, and custom executors.
    - Vended Tools
      - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/index.md): Pre-built tools included in the SDK for common agent tasks like file operations, shell commands, HTTP requests, and persistent notes.
      - [edit](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/edit/index.md): Use the edit vended tool to let a Strands agent make surgical, in-place changes to a text file by replacing an exact, unique string with the new content.
      - [file-editor](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/file-editor/index.md): Use the file editor vended tool to let a Strands agent view, create, and make targeted edits to files on disk, for coding agents and config management work.
      - [read](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/read/index.md): Use the read vended tool to let a Strands agent read a file as numbered text lines, with paging for large files, or as an image or document media block.
      - [write](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/write/index.md): Use the write vended tool to let a Strands agent create a new text file or overwrite an existing one with the full provided content in a single tool call.
      - [http-request](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/http-request/index.md): Use the HTTP request vended tool to let a Strands agent call external APIs and fetch web content, with any HTTP method, custom headers, and request bodies.
      - [notebook](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/notebook/index.md): Give a Strands agent persistent notebooks to plan multi-step tasks and track progress. Notebook state lives in agent state and persists with session management.
      - [shell](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/shell/index.md): Let a Strands agent run shell commands: TypeScript's bash keeps a persistent host session, while shell runs each stateless command through the agent's sandbox.
      - [mcp-router](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/mcp-router/index.md): Let a Strands agent connect to MCP servers at runtime, list and call their tools, and disconnect, limited to a developer-configured allowlist of servers.
      - [sleep](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/sleep/index.md): Pause a Strands agent for a bounded number of seconds. Cancelling the invocation aborts the sleep, and the developer, not the model, sets the maximum duration.
      - [handoff-to-user](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/handoff-to-user/index.md): Let a Strands agent pause its loop and hand a message to the user for confirmation or input, then resume with the reply via the interrupt and resume mechanism.
      - [stop](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/stop/index.md): Let the model end a Strands agent loop deliberately with an optional final message. A cooperative stop: tools requested in the same turn still run to the end.
      - [web-fetch](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/web-fetch/index.md): Fetch an HTTP(S) URL and return its content to a Strands agent, either as clean markdown or through an analyst agent that answers a prompt about the page.
      - [a2a-client](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/a2a-client/index.md): Let a Strands agent discover remote A2A protocol agents and send them messages, limited to an endpoint allowlist with optional per-endpoint authentication.
      - [python-repl](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/python-repl/index.md): Run model-generated Python through a Strands agent's sandbox. Each call starts a fresh interpreter, while files written to the sandbox persist across calls.
      - [subagent](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/subagent/index.md): Delegate a self-contained task to a child agent that runs in its own context and returns a final report, keeping intermediate work out of the parent's context.
      - [swarm](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/swarm/index.md): Let a Strands agent spin up a team of specialized sub-agents that collaborate through handoffs, with axis policies, presets, and limits you configure.
      - [graph](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/tools/vended-tools/graph/index.md): Let a Strands agent design and run a team of sub-agents as a directed acyclic graph. Root nodes start in parallel, and each node receives its upstream outputs.
  - Memory
    - [test-memory-store](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/memory/test-memory-store/index.md): A zero-infrastructure memory store backed by a local JSON file: no cloud account, lexical recall, and memories that survive across sessions.
    - [file-memory-store](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/memory/file-memory-store/index.md): Persist agent memories as markdown files on any Storage backend (local, S3, or custom): one file per topic, pluggable search, and topic-aware extraction.
    - [bedrock-knowledge-base](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/memory/bedrock-knowledge-base/index.md): Back agent memory with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases: semantic search over a managed vector store and document ingestion for CUSTOM and S3 data sources.
  - Plugins
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/plugins/index.md): Extend agent behavior with plugins. Add steering, guardrails, and custom capabilities that hook into the agent lifecycle.
    - [skills](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/plugins/skills/index.md): Give Strands agents on-demand access to specialized instructions with the AgentSkills plugin. Progressive disclosure keeps the system prompt lean.
    - [context-offloader](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/plugins/context-offloader/index.md): Prevent large tool results from consuming the context window. ContextOffloader stores oversized results externally and leaves retrievable references.
    - [context-injector](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/plugins/context-injector/index.md): Fold real-time text into the model input before each call with the ContextInjector plugin: a clock, environment facts, or a lookup, not stored in history.
    - [todos](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/plugins/todos/index.md): Give the agent a task list it maintains with todo_write and keeps in view: the Todos plugin re-surfaces the current plan at intervals during a long run.
    - [goal-loop](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/plugins/goal-loop/index.md): Iterative refinement plugin that validates agent responses against a goal, looping with feedback until satisfied.
    - [genai-prices-estimator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/plugins/genai-prices-estimator/index.md): Estimate what a request cost in USD: the GenAIPricesEstimator plugin prices each model's token usage with the genai-prices package and streams the estimate after every model call.
    - [custom-plugins](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/plugins/custom-plugins/index.md): Write your own Strands plugin: attach it to an agent, register hooks and tools, manage state, and initialize asynchronously.
  - Interventions
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/interventions/index.md): A composable control layer for authorization, guardrails, and steering with typed actions, ordered evaluation, and short-circuiting.
    - [Human in the loop](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/interventions/human-in-the-loop/index.md): Gate agent tool execution behind human approval. Configurable modes for CLI, web, and custom UIs with optional session trust.
    - [cedar-authorization](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/interventions/cedar-authorization/index.md): Control which tools an agent can invoke using Cedar policies. Enforce identity-aware access control, role-based permissions, and rate limits at the tool-call boundary.
    - [dogwood-authorization](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/interventions/dogwood-authorization/index.md): Gate agent tool calls with Dogwood policies: Cedar-style access control plus temporal rules that decide based on what the agent already did this session.
    - [steering](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/interventions/steering/index.md): Guide agents with just-in-time contextual feedback instead of front-loaded prompts. Python uses plugins; TypeScript uses the interventions framework.
  - Sandbox
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/sandbox/index.md): Configure where an agent runs shell commands, executes code, and accesses a filesystem. Swap between Docker, SSH, or custom environments.
    - [available-sandboxes](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/sandbox/available-sandboxes/index.md): Use the built-in Docker and SSH sandboxes, drive a sandbox from your own code, and stream output from long-running commands.
    - [custom-sandbox](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/sandbox/custom-sandbox/index.md): Target an execution environment the built-in sandboxes do not cover: extend PosixShellSandbox or implement the Sandbox interface directly.
  - Multi-agent
    - [agent-to-agent](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/multi-agent/agent-to-agent/index.md): Connect Strands agents across platforms with the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. Serve agents over A2A and call remote agents from your own.
    - [a2a-server-configuration](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/multi-agent/a2a-server-configuration/index.md): Reference for configuring a Strands A2A server: constructor options, custom task stores and request-handler components, and path-based mounting for load-balanced deployments.
    - [agents-as-tools](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/multi-agent/agents-as-tools/index.md): Wrap specialized Strands agents as callable tools so an orchestrator agent can delegate tasks to domain experts in a hierarchical pattern.
    - [swarm](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/multi-agent/swarm/index.md): Build self-organizing agent teams with the Strands Swarm pattern. Agents collaborate through autonomous handoffs, shared context, and working memory.
    - [graph](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/multi-agent/graph/index.md): Orchestrate multi-agent systems with the Strands Graph pattern: deterministic DAG or cyclic execution, conditional edges, and nested agents.
    - [graph-components](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/multi-agent/graph-components/index.md): Reference for the Strands Graph building blocks: GraphNode, GraphEdge, and GraphBuilder in Python, and the node, edge, and constructor types in TypeScript.
    - [workflow](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/multi-agent/workflow/index.md): Coordinate Strands agents in application code. Pass results between steps, handle failures, and choose when to use a Graph or the vended graph tool.
  - Streaming
    - [async-iterators](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/streaming/async-iterators/index.md): Stream Strands agent events asynchronously with async iterators. Process text, tool usage, and lifecycle events in FastAPI and other async frameworks.
    - [callback-handlers](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/streaming/callback-handlers/index.md): Intercept Strands agent events in Python with callback handlers. Monitor streaming text and tool usage in real time or format custom output.
    - [events](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/streaming/events/index.md): Reference for every event a Strands agent stream emits: lifecycle, model output, tool activity, and multi-agent coordination events, plus how to serialize them.
  - Voice
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/index.md): Build Strands agents that take input while they respond. BidiAgent streams audio and text both ways, accepts image input, and runs your tools.
    - [quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/quickstart/index.md): Talk to a Strands BidiAgent through your microphone and speakers: call a tool, talk over its reply, cancel echo, and end the conversation by voice.
    - [agent](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/agent/index.md): Create and manage live conversations with BidiAgent. Send input, receive output events, control the lifecycle, and preserve history across connection restarts.
    - Models
      - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/models/index.md): Realtime models for BidiAgent: the providers Strands supports, and the configuration, audio, and connection behavior they share.
      - [bedrock](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/models/bedrock/index.md): Configure Amazon Nova Sonic for BidiAgent: set AWS credentials, choose a voice, tune turn detection, and preserve context across connection restarts.
      - [google](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/models/google/index.md): Configure Google Gemini Live for BidiAgent: set credentials, choose a voice and audio settings, tune turn detection, and manage connection restarts.
      - [realtime](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/models/openai/realtime/index.md): Configure OpenAI Realtime for BidiAgent: set credentials, choose a voice and transcription model, tune turn detection, and manage connection restarts.
      - [live](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/models/openai/live/index.md): Configure OpenAI Live for BidiAgent: set credentials, choose voice and backend models, configure audio and tools, and understand experimental event boundaries.
    - [tools](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/tools/index.md): Give BidiAgent tools that run while the conversation continues. Register tools, understand concurrent execution, and let users end a conversation.
    - [io](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/io/index.md): Connect microphones, speakers, terminals, and WebSockets to BidiAgent. Combine input and output streams, configure audio, and build custom adapters.
    - [content](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/content/index.md): Send text, images, and streaming audio to BidiAgent. Combine ordered content blocks, use dictionary forms, and understand how inputs become model messages.
    - [events](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/events/index.md): Consume stream events to handle audio, text, tool results, barge-in, and connection restarts. Understand event payloads, ordering, and completion.
    - [hooks](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/hooks/index.md): Register BidiAgent hooks to observe history changes, inspect tool calls, and react to response and connection events.
    - [session-management](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/session-management/index.md): Save and resume BidiAgent conversations with SnapshotSessionManager. Choose when to persist state, restore saved history, and work with snapshot checkpoints.
    - [interrupts](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/interrupts/index.md): Interrupt support for BidiAgent is in development. This page will cover pausing and resuming bidirectional conversations when interrupt support is available.
    - [observability](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/bidi/observability/index.md): Trace, measure, and log BidiAgent sessions: connection lifecycle, time to first audio, barge-ins, per-modality token usage, and restarts.
  - [Conversation management](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/agents/conversation-management/index.md): Keep long agent conversations within token limits using sliding window and summarizing conversation managers in the Strands Agents SDK.
  - Experimental
    - [agent-config](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/experimental/agent-config/index.md): Create Strands agents from JSON files or dictionaries with the experimental config_to_agent function, including tool loading and model settings.
- Reference
  - [versioning-and-support](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/sdk/versioning-and-support/index.md): How the Strands Harness SDK versions releases: semantic versioning guarantees, experimental feature policies, and deprecation timelines explained.
  - [API reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/api/python/index.md): The full API reference for the Strands Agents Python SDK: every class, method, tool, model provider, and hook with complete signatures.
  - [API reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/api/typescript/index.md): The full API reference for the Strands Agents TypeScript SDK: every class, interface, function, and type across the SDK packages.

## Shell

- Get started
  - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/index.md): Strands Shell is an in-process shell sandbox that gives agents a fast, isolated command line with filesystem, network, and credential mediation built in.
  - [quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/quickstart/index.md): Install Strands Shell and run your first sandboxed command through the MCP server, the Python API, or the Node.js API in just a few minutes.
  - [how-it-works](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/how-it-works/index.md): Why Strands Shell isolates at the process instead of the kernel, how the Kernel boundary and shell engine fit together, and where that tradeoff holds.
- Guides
  - [Configure the sandbox](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/configuration/index.md): Bind host directories, inject credentials per URL, set the network allowlist, and tune resource limits for Strands Shell, in code or from a TOML file.
  - [Run the MCP server](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/mcp-server/index.md): Expose Strands Shell to any MCP-compatible agent over stdio, with four sandboxed tools and optional nested MCP servers surfaced as Lua modules.
  - [Inspect the configuration](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/inspecting-configuration/index.md): Read back how a Strands Shell was configured (binds, credentials, allowlist, limits) from a read-only snapshot that never exposes credential secrets.
- Components
  - [Commands](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/commands/index.md): The full command inventory in Strands Shell, with supported flags, shell builtins, and known divergences from GNU and BSD coreutils behavior.
  - [Shell language and builtins](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/shell-language/index.md): The shell language Strands Shell supports (pipelines, redirections, control flow, expansions) and its builtins, with the behaviors that diverge from Bash.
  - [Lua scripting](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/lua-scripting/index.md): Run sandboxed Lua 5.4 inside Strands Shell for multi-step transforms and structured data, and call nested MCP servers as Lua modules from a script.
- Security
  - [Security model](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/security/index.md): How the Kernel boundary mediates filesystem, network, and credential access, what Strands Shell guarantees, and when to add OS-level isolation.
- Reference
  - [Reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/shell/reference/index.md): The one place to look up Strands Shell's surface, the command-line interface, the Python and Node.js API, the command inventory, the configuration and TOML schema, and the MCP server tools.

## Box

- Get started
  - [Get started with Box](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/quickstart/index.md): Install Box and run Claude Code in a box in one of your own projects.
  - [Install Box](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/install/index.md): Install, upgrade, or remove a Box release.
  - [How Box works](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/how-box-works/index.md): How the box, profiles, packs, starters, policy, and credentials fit together.
- Use Box
  - [Profiles](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/profiles/index.md): What a profile decides, where it lives, and how to change what the agent can reach.
  - [Packs](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/packs/index.md): What a pack is, where it lives, and how to write one for an agent, a tool, or shared settings.
  - [Policies](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/policies/index.md): What a policy checks, where a run's rules come from, and how to write your own.
  - [Starters](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/starters/index.md): Make a profile from a starter, and write starters so a team gets one standard setup.
  - [Box plugins](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/plugins/index.md): What a plugin is, how to read a key from a password manager with one, and how to write one.
  - [Credentials](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/credentials/index.md): Where a route's key comes from: a shell variable, AWS credentials, the credentials daemon, or a password manager.
- Help
  - [Troubleshooting](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/troubleshooting/index.md): What a box error means, and how to fix it.
  - [What a box does not protect](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/limitations/index.md): What a box doesn't protect you from, and what to check before you trust a run.
  - [Where file rules apply](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/file-rules/index.md): Which processes a policy's file rules check, and how to keep a file from every process.
- Reference
  - [box command reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/cli/index.md): Every box command, flag, environment variable, and exit status.
  - [Profile reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/profiles/index.md): Every key a profile can hold, and the rules that profiles and packs share.
  - [Pack reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/packs/index.md): Every key that only a pack writes.
  - [Starter reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/starters/index.md): Every key a starter and a policy starter can hold.
  - [Plugin reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/plugins/index.md): Every key a plugin can hold, and the rules for plugins.
  - [Policy reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/policies/index.md): How box joins a run's policy, and each rule it writes.
  - [Box config reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/box-config/index.md): The config.toml tables that set the starter and policy menus and the banner for every profile.
  - [Where Box keeps its files](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/files/index.md): What each folder under ~/.strands/box holds, and where your own packs and policies go.
  - [Policy language](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/policy/index.md): Understand how Box loads, evaluates, and records Dogwood policy decisions.
  - [Policy action reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/policy-actions/index.md): Look up every Box policy action, its input fields, and its enforcement point.
  - [Strands Shell reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/shell/index.md): Look up shell invocation forms, commands, host programs, policy fields, and exit statuses.
  - [Python in a box](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/python/index.md): Run Python through Monty and control its file and network operations with policy.
  - [macOS requirements](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/macos-requirements/index.md): Check the macOS release package, program dependencies, sandbox startup, and requirements for optional native filesystem policy.
  - [Linux requirements](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/linux-requirements/index.md): Check Linux libraries, permissions to create the sandbox, startup errors, and tested configurations.
  - [Message codes](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/message-codes/index.md): Read the message format Box writes to stderr, and what each message code means and asks you to do.
- Box Core
  - [Run an agent with box.toml](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/core/quickstart/index.md): Run the Strands CLI under box.toml and policy.dw with Box Core, observe a refused write, and permit it.
  - [box.toml configuration reference](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/configuration/index.md): Configure every Box input, process, filesystem grant, credential, MCP server, and telemetry target.
  - [Security: what Box governs, and what you own](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/security/index.md): Understand Box enforcement tiers, trust boundaries, operator duties, and policy limitations.
  - Guides
    - [Write a policy and read what it decided](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/write-a-policy/index.md): Write permit and forbid rules, observe a refusal, and inspect Box decision records.
    - [Write policy for shell commands](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/write-shell-policy/index.md): Control shell commands, file operations, host programs, and built programs with policy.
    - [MCP server configuration](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/add-an-mcp-server/index.md): Configure local stdio and remote HTTP MCP servers for a boxed agent.
    - [Write policy for an MCP server](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/write-mcp-policy/index.md): Permit and restrict MCP server tools and arguments with Dogwood policy.
    - [Egress credential configuration](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/network-and-credentials/index.md): Bind credentials to permitted network destinations with Box configuration.
    - [Telemetry](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/record-telemetry/index.md): Configure decision and workload telemetry targets, filters, and records.
    - [Tool grammars](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/tool-grammars/index.md): Experimental. Describe a program such as git as actions and effects, and write one rule for every spelling of a command.
    - [Experimental native filesystem policy](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/security/native-filesystem-policy/index.md): Enable and configure experimental native filesystem policy on macOS and Linux ARM64.
  - Deploy
    - [Run a Strands Agents SDK agent in a box](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/run-strands-harness/index.md): Run a Strands Agents SDK agent in Box and control its commands and files with policy.
    - [Collect the Strands CLI's traces and metrics](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/strands-cli-telemetry/index.md): Send Strands CLI traces and metrics to the Box records file and inspect them together.
    - [Run Box on Amazon EKS](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/deploy-to-eks/index.md): Deploy Box as an Amazon EKS Job, verify policy enforcement, and optionally run Claude Code with Pod Identity.
    - [Run a Box shipment agent on AgentCore Runtime](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/deploy-to-agentcore-runtime/index.md): Package, deploy, invoke, and verify a Box-contained shipment agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime.
    - [Run Strands Box on Google Cloud](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/guides/deploy-to-google-cloud/index.md): Deploy a Strands agent with Gemini to a Google Compute Engine VM and verify Box's deployment retry cooldown.
    - [Cloud deployment profiles](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/box/reference/cloud-deployments/index.md): Configure and check AgentCore Runtime and Lambda MicroVM deployments using the shared Linux requirements.

## Evals SDK

- Get started
  - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/index.md): Validate your agent before you ship: evaluators, detectors, red teaming, and simulators in one SDK.
  - [quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/quickstart/index.md): Run your first Strands evaluation: install the SDK, write an experiment, score an agent with a built-in evaluator, and read the results.
  - [how-evaluation-works](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/how-evaluation-works/index.md): Understand how a Strands evaluation fits together: an experiment of cases, a task that produces output, evaluators that score it, and detectors that diagnose.
  - [Evaluate with AI](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/eval-sop/index.md): Point an AI assistant at your agent and it runs the whole evaluation: plan, generate test data, score with the Evals SDK, and write a report.
- Build guides
  - [experiment_generator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/experiment_generator/index.md): Generate evaluation experiments automatically with ExperimentGenerator: LLM-created test cases, rubrics, and topic-based coverage for your agent.
  - [topic_planning](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/topic_planning/index.md): Distribute generated test cases across diverse, non-overlapping topics with num_topics or the TopicPlanner utility for broad agent coverage.
- Run guides
  - [eval_task](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/how-to/eval_task/index.md): Write evaluation task functions with the @eval_task decorator, which handles telemetry, session mapping, and result normalization for you.
  - [result_caching](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/how-to/result_caching/index.md): Cache task execution results with EvaluationDataStore so you can iterate on evaluators without re-invoking expensive or slow agent calls.
  - [experiment_management](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/how-to/experiment_management/index.md): Organize evaluation test cases into experiments: use metadata for filtering, group related cases, and adapt experiments across agent versions.
  - [serialization](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/how-to/serialization/index.md): Save, load, version, and share evaluation work with JSON serialization for Strands Evals experiments and evaluation reports.
  - [trace_providers](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/how-to/trace_providers/index.md): Evaluate production agent traces without re-running them: fetch execution data from CloudWatch, Langfuse, or OpenSearch with trace providers.
  - [agentcore_evaluation_dashboard](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/how-to/agentcore_evaluation_dashboard/index.md): Evaluate Strands agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations: managed evaluators, online and on-demand evaluation, and CloudWatch dashboards.
- Components
  - Evaluators
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/index.md): Choose and run a Strands evaluator: LLM-judge and deterministic scorers for output quality, safety, multimodal, and agentic behavior.
    - Quality
      - [output_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/output_evaluator/index.md): Score agent responses against a custom rubric with OutputEvaluator, an LLM-as-a-judge evaluator for safety, relevance, accuracy, and completeness.
      - [trajectory_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/trajectory_evaluator/index.md): Judge the sequence of tool calls and actions an agent took with TrajectoryEvaluator, including exact, in-order, and any-order matching tools.
      - [interactions_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/interactions_evaluator/index.md): Evaluate multi-agent workflows step by step with InteractionsEvaluator, scoring each interaction with node-specific rubrics and dependencies.
      - [helpfulness_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/helpfulness_evaluator/index.md): Measure how helpful agent responses are from the user's perspective with HelpfulnessEvaluator and its seven-level scoring scale.
      - [faithfulness_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/faithfulness_evaluator/index.md): Detect hallucinations with FaithfulnessEvaluator by checking whether agent statements stay grounded in the preceding conversation history.
      - [correctness_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/correctness_evaluator/index.md): Check the factual correctness of agent responses with CorrectnessEvaluator, from conversation context alone or against an expected reference answer.
      - [coherence_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/coherence_evaluator/index.md): Assess the logical consistency and flow of agent responses with CoherenceEvaluator, an LLM judge with a five-level scoring rubric.
      - [conciseness_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/conciseness_evaluator/index.md): Catch verbose agent responses with ConcisenessEvaluator, which scores how efficiently a response communicates on a three-level scale.
      - [response_relevance_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/response_relevance_evaluator/index.md): Verify agent responses address what the user actually asked with ResponseRelevanceEvaluator and its five-level relevance scale.
    - Safety
      - [harmfulness_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/harmfulness_evaluator/index.md): Screen agent responses for dangerous or offensive content with the binary harmful or not-harmful classification of HarmfulnessEvaluator.
      - [refusal_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/refusal_evaluator/index.md): Detect when an agent refuses a user request with RefusalEvaluator, which separates true refusals from merely irrelevant responses.
      - [stereotyping_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/stereotyping_evaluator/index.md): Flag biased or stereotypical content in agent responses with StereotypingEvaluator, including stereotypes the response later rejects.
    - Multimodal
      - [multimodal_output_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/multimodal_output_evaluator/index.md): Evaluate agent outputs on image and document tasks with MultimodalOutputEvaluator, which judges responses against a custom rubric using an MLLM.
      - [multimodal_overall_quality_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/multimodal_overall_quality_evaluator/index.md): Score overall response quality on image tasks with MultimodalOverallQualityEvaluator: visual accuracy, instruction adherence, and coherence.
      - [multimodal_correctness_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/multimodal_correctness_evaluator/index.md): Fact-check agent responses against image content with MultimodalCorrectnessEvaluator: objects, counts, colors, positions, and readable text.
      - [multimodal_faithfulness_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/multimodal_faithfulness_evaluator/index.md): Catch visual hallucinations with MultimodalFaithfulnessEvaluator, which checks agent responses for invented details not grounded in the image.
      - [multimodal_instruction_following_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/multimodal_instruction_following_evaluator/index.md): Verify responses on image tasks satisfy explicit constraints like count, format, and scope with MultimodalInstructionFollowingEvaluator.
    - Agentic
      - [instruction_following_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/instruction_following_evaluator/index.md): Evaluate whether agent responses comply with explicit prompt instructions using the binary scoring of InstructionFollowingEvaluator.
      - [goal_success_rate_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/goal_success_rate_evaluator/index.md): Determine whether an agent accomplished all user goals across an entire conversation session with the GoalSuccessRateEvaluator's binary score.
      - [failure_communication_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/failure_communication_evaluator/index.md): Rate how clearly your agent explains tool failures to users with FailureCommunicationEvaluator: clarity, actionability, transparency, and tone.
      - [partial_completion_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/partial_completion_evaluator/index.md): Measure the fraction of a user goal an agent achieved with PartialCompletionEvaluator, a continuous 0.0 to 1.0 score for multi-step tasks.
      - [recovery_strategy_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/recovery_strategy_evaluator/index.md): Score how well an agent recovers from tool failures with RecoveryStrategyEvaluator: alternative approaches, retries, and strategy variation.
      - [tool_selection_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/tool_selection_evaluator/index.md): Check that your agent picks the right tool at the right time with ToolSelectionAccuracyEvaluator, which judges each tool call in context.
      - [tool_parameter_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/tool_parameter_evaluator/index.md): Verify tool call parameters are grounded in conversation context, not hallucinated, with per-call checks from ToolParameterAccuracyEvaluator.
    - Skill
      - [skill_selection_accuracy_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/skill_selection_accuracy_evaluator/index.md): Judge whether each skill your agent chose to load was the right call with SkillSelectionAccuracyEvaluator, one binary verdict per invoked skill.
      - [skill_instruction_following_evaluator](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/skill_instruction_following_evaluator/index.md): Measure how fully your agent followed each invoked skill's steps with SkillInstructionFollowingEvaluator, a five-point rating grounded in per-step evidence.
    - [Deterministic](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/deterministic_evaluators/index.md): Run fast, code-based checks without LLM judges: deterministic evaluators match outputs, verify tool calls, and compare state for CI/CD pipelines.
    - [Structured output similarity](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/structured_output_evaluator/index.md): Score structured agent output field by field with StructuredOutputSimilarity, a deterministic evaluator with order-independent lists and per-field metrics.
    - [Typed rubric](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/typed_rubric_evaluator/index.md): Score agent output against yes/no, scale, and choice questions with TypedRubricEvaluator, using a decision model's probabilities instead of judge text.
    - [Custom](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/evaluators/custom_evaluator/index.md): Build domain-specific evaluation logic by extending the Evaluator base class: custom scoring, external services, and specialized data analysis.
  - Detectors
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/detectors/index.md): Find out why your agent failed: detectors analyze execution traces to detect failures, classify root causes, and recommend concrete fixes.
    - [failure_detection](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/detectors/failure_detection/index.md): Detect semantic failures in agent traces with detect_failures: hallucinations, tool misuse, and policy violations across a 20+ category taxonomy.
    - [root_cause_analysis](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/detectors/root_cause_analysis/index.md): Trace failure chains in agent sessions with analyze_root_cause: classify causality, assess propagation impact, and get fix recommendations.
