    - [diagnosis](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/detectors/diagnosis/index.md): Run the full failure diagnosis pipeline with diagnose_session: detect failures, analyze root causes, and get deduplicated fix recommendations.
  - Simulators
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/simulators/index.md): Evaluate agents with dynamic simulators that drive multi-turn conversations and generate realistic tool responses beyond static test cases.
    - [user_simulation](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/simulators/user_simulation/index.md): Simulate realistic end users with ActorSimulator to evaluate agents in dynamic, goal-oriented multi-turn conversations without scripted inputs.
    - [customize_user_simulation](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/simulators/customize_user_simulation/index.md): Customize ActorSimulator user simulations with custom actor profiles, system prompts, additional tools, and alternative models for evaluation.
    - [tool_simulation](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/simulators/tool_simulation/index.md): Replace real tool execution with LLM-generated, schema-validated responses using ToolSimulator to evaluate agents without live infrastructure.
  - Red teaming
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/red-teaming/index.md): Probe a Strands agent's safety by running adversarial attack strategies against it and scoring whether each attack breached its guardrails.
    - [quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/red-teaming/quickstart/index.md): Run an adversarial red-team experiment against a Strands agent end to end, generating attack cases, running a strategy, and reading which attacks breached.
    - [strategies](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/red-teaming/strategies/index.md): The built-in red-team attack strategies (Crescendo, GOAT, PAIR, Bad Likert Judge, SequentialBreak), their parameters, and when to use each.
    - [custom_cases](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/red-teaming/custom_cases/index.md): Hand-author RedTeamCase objects for domain-specific red-team risks, and write success_criteria the LLM judge can apply reliably.
    - [custom_task](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/red-teaming/custom_task/index.md): Replace the built-in red-team task with your own, to wrap the target in a guardrail, add a check between turns, or build the target yourself.
    - [evaluators](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/red-teaming/evaluators/index.md): How AttackSuccessEvaluator scores a red-team attack from 0.0 to 1.0, what counts as a breach, and how to tune the threshold.
    - [reading_the_report](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/red-teaming/reading_the_report/index.md): Understand what a RedTeamReport prints, how to read the breach matrix and per-attack table, and what to do when an attack breaches.
  - Optimization
    - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/optimization/index.md): Improve a Strands agent's prompts, components, and settings from your own evaluation cases, and get back a reviewable diff plus the values to apply.
    - [quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/optimization/quickstart/index.md): Optimize a Strands support-ticket triage agent end to end, rewriting its system prompt and tuning its temperature against a rubric judge and a token budget.
    - [tunables](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/optimization/tunables/index.md): Mark prompts, files, skills, tool descriptions, numbers, and components as tunable, including context strategies, component swaps, and multi-agent factories.
    - [entry_routes](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/optimization/entry_routes/index.md): Optimize an agent from a Python factory, your own task function, a Strands harness config file, or an exported agent file, and see what each route can't tune.
    - [objectives](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/optimization/objectives/index.md): Tell the optimizer what "better" means with objectives and constraints over evaluator scores and token usage, and size the rollout budget for a run.
    - [search](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/optimization/search/index.md): Choose which proposer changes which part of an agent, opt in to Thompson sampling for choices, and change the model that rewrites text during an optimization run.
    - [results](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/optimization/results/index.md): Read an optimization run's summary, diff, effects, validation pick, and test report, apply the champion, and resume a run that was stopped.
  - [chaos_testing](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/chaos_testing/index.md): Test agent resilience by injecting controlled tool failures with ChaosPlugin: simulate timeouts, network errors, and corrupted responses safely.
- CLI
  - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/cli/index.md): Run agent evaluations from the command line with strands-evals: execute experiments, generate test cases, render reports, and diagnose failures in CI.
  - [run](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/cli/run/index.md): Execute an evaluation experiment or a one-off ad-hoc case from the command line with strands-evals run: agent factories, caching, and CI exit codes.
  - [generate](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/cli/generate/index.md): Generate evaluation experiments from the command line with strands-evals generate: LLM-created test cases from a context description, with or without topics.
  - [diagnose](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/cli/diagnose/index.md): Detect failures and analyze root causes from the command line: strands-evals diagnose scores a Session JSON, and fetch pulls one from a trace provider.
  - [report](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/cli/report/index.md): Render evaluation reports and schema-check experiment files from the command line with strands-evals report and validate, including stdin piping for CI.
  - [ui](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/user-guide/evals-sdk/cli/ui/index.md): Serve a local page over a directory of evaluation files with strands-evals ui: browse reports, sessions, and optimizer runs, and edit cases in place.

## Contribute

- [contribute](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/contribute/index.md): Ways to contribute to the Strands Agents ecosystem: fix bugs in the core SDK, improve the documentation, or build and publish extensions.
- Contribution Types
  - [core-sdk](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/contribute/contributing/core-sdk/index.md): Contribute to the Strands core SDK for Python and TypeScript: find open issues, set up your development environment, and submit changes for review.
  - [documentation](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/contribute/contributing/documentation/index.md): Contribute to Strands Agents documentation: run the Astro site locally, use the docs agent skills, and submit anything from typo fixes to new guides.
  - [feature-proposals](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/contribute/contributing/feature-proposals/index.md): Propose significant features for the Strands Harness SDK: when to write a design document, what to include, and how the review process works.
  - [extensions](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/contribute/contributing/extensions/index.md): Package and publish your own Strands components: share tools, model providers, and session managers so other developers can install them.

## Community

- Labs
  - [labs](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/index.md): Explore Strands Labs, the experimental arm of Strands Agents: open source projects covering robotics, world models, agentic benchmarks, harness optimization, audio processing, and decision models.
  - Strands Decider
    - Get started
      - [Overview](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/overview/index.md): Strands Decider is a top-performing System One decision model from the Strands Agents team and AWS.
      - [Quickstart](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/quickstart/index.md): Install Strands Decider, serve it, and use it as a model router inside a Strands agent.
      - [Introduction](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/introduction/index.md): Understand System One models and the three question types Strands Decider supports.
    - Models
      - [Inference server](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/inference/index.md): Serve Strands Decider over HTTP: install, endpoints, devices, and request shapes.
      - [Models](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/models/index.md): Compare the Strands Decider v2 and v1 models and pick the right one.
      - V2 Models
        - [E2B-gemma4 v2](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/models/e2b-gemma4-v2/index.md): The v2 model on Gemma 4 E2B.
        - [E4B-gemma4 v2](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/models/e4b-gemma4-v2/index.md): The v2 model on Gemma 4 E4B.
        - [12B-gemma4 v2](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/models/12b-gemma4-v2/index.md): The v2 model on Gemma 4 12B.

        - [31B-gemma4 v2](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/models/31b-gemma4-v2/index.md): The v2 model on Gemma 4 31B.

        - [E4B-gemma4](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/models/e4b-gemma4/index.md): The mid-size Gemma 4 v1 checkpoint.
        - [12B-gemma4](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/models/12b-gemma4/index.md): The dense Gemma 4 12B v1 checkpoint.

    - Deployment
      - [Local](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/deployment/local/index.md): Run Strands Decider on your own machine or an on-prem box.

      - [Lambda](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/deployment/lambda/index.md): Deploy Strands Decider behind an AWS Lambda function.

    - Training
      - [Understanding Strands Decider](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/understanding/index.md): The shape of Decider: three question types, the v2 token readout and the v1 pointer head, calibration, and what the models train on.
      - [Train a model](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/training/index.md): Train a v2 model in three steps: convert your rows, train one config, and export the result.
      - [Data card](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/labs/strands-decider/data-card/index.md): The v2 training data: how many rows, how they were made, what they are about, and sample rows.
- Learning
  - [Lesson 1: How agents really work](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/how-agents-really-work/index.md): A ground-up look at the agent loop: how a model, a set of tools, and a running context combine to let an agent reason, act, and observe until a task is done.
  - [Lesson 2: Switching model providers](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/switching-model-providers/index.md): This covers model providers: how Strands abstracts the underlying LLM so your agent logic stays the same regardless of which model you're calling.
  - [Lesson 3: Give your agent tools using MCP](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/give-your-agent-tools-using-mcp/index.md): This chapter covers MCP and how it changes the way you think about equipping your agent with capabilities.
  - [Lesson 4: Adding callbacks & response streaming](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/adding-callbacks-and-response-streaming/index.md): This chapter is about making the agent's work visible while it's happening, not just dumping a final answer after 15 seconds of silence.
  - [Lesson 5: Control your agent with hooks](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/control-your-agent-with-hooks/index.md): Hooks fire at the same event points as callbacks (before/after tool calls, before/after model calls, cycle boundaries) but they can modify or cancel what's about to happen.
  - [Lesson 6: Agent plugins & skills](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/agent-plugins-and-skills/index.md): Individual tools solve individual problems. But some capabilities require multiple tools working together with specific hooks and prompt instructions to function correctly. That's what a plugin is: a packaged bundle of tools + hooks + system prompt additions that you attach to an agent as a unit.
  - [Lesson 7: Improve agent reliability with Strands steering](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/improve-agent-reliability-with-strands-steering/index.md): System prompts set the agent's general personality and rules, but they're blunt. You can't easily say 'only for this next tool call, format the output as JSON' or 'when the user mentions billing, always check their account status first' without bloating the prompt with conditionals the model has to parse every single turn.
  - [Lesson 8: Context engineering & conversation management](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/context-engineering-and-conversation-management/index.md): Every turn, the model receives the full conversation history plus system prompt plus tool results. That window fills up fast. Once it does, you either hit token limits, start paying significantly more per request, or the model starts missing information buried in the middle.
  - [Lesson 9: Persistent memory with session managers](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/persistent-memory-with-session-managers/index.md): Without persistence, every conversation starts from zero. The agent has no memory of prior interactions, no accumulated knowledge about the user, no awareness of decisions made yesterday. Session managers handle the storage and retrieval of conversation state so continuity works automatically.
  - [Lesson 10: Multi-agent patterns: agents as tools](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/multi-agent-patterns-agents-as-tools/index.md): This is where we cross from single-agent patterns into multi-agent orchestration, and we start with the most intuitive version: an agent that can call other agents the same way it calls any other tool.
  - [Lesson 11: Multi-agent patterns: graph workflows](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/multi-agent-patterns-graph-workflows/index.md): Some workflows have a fixed structure: step A feeds into step B, step B branches based on a condition, both branches converge at step C. You don't want the model deciding whether to run step B. You want it guaranteed.
  - [Lesson 12: Multi-agent patterns: agent swarms](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/multi-agent-patterns-agent-swarms/index.md): In a swarm, multiple agents share a workspace or communication channel. Each agent has its own tools, its own prompt, its own specialization.
  - [Lesson 13: Evaluating agents](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/evaluating-agents/index.md): Agent evaluation is harder than traditional software testing. The output is non-deterministic.
  - [Lesson 14: Deploying agents to the cloud](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/docs/learning/deploying-agents-to-the-cloud/index.md): We'll deploy an agent to AWS using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AgentCore is a collection of components for building, deploying and operating agents in production. The main components we will focus on in this video is AgentCore Runtime and AgentCore Memory.

- [Strands Agents TypeScript SDK: Build AI Agents in TypeScript](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/strands-agents-typescript-sdk/index.md): The Strands Agents TypeScript SDK brings the model-driven approach to the TypeScript ecosystem. Build type-safe AI agents that run in Node.js and the browser.
- [Simulate realistic users to evaluate multi-turn AI agents in Strands Evals](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/simulate-realistic-users-multi-turn-agents-strands-evals/index.md): ActorSimulator in the Strands Evals SDK enables teams to test conversational agents through realistic, goal-driven simulated users rather than relying on static test cases or manual testing.
- [Evaluating AI agents for production: A practical guide to Strands Evals](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/evaluating-ai-agents-practical-guide-strands-evals/index.md): Learn how to systematically evaluate AI agents using Strands Evals, covering core concepts like cases, experiments, evaluators, multi-turn simulation capabilities, and practical integration patterns for production deployment.
- [How Steering Hooks Achieved 100% Agent Accuracy Where Prompts and Workflows Failed](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/steering-accuracy-beats-prompts-workflows/index.md): Steering hooks achieved a 100% accuracy pass rate across 600 evaluation runs, compared to 82.5% for simple prompt-based instructions and 80.8% for graph-based workflows.
- [Runtime Guardrails for Strands Agents with Agent Control](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/strands-agents-with-agent-control/index.md): Define what your Strands agents can and can't do at runtime, without changing a line of agent code.
- [Introducing Strands Labs: Get hands-on today with state-of-the-art, experimental approaches to agentic development](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/introducing-strands-labs/index.md): Strands Labs is a new GitHub organization designed to give developers the ability to get hands-on with experimental, state-of-the-art approaches to agentic AI development.
- [Building intelligent physical AI: From edge to cloud with Strands Agents, Bedrock AgentCore, Claude 4.5, NVIDIA GR00T, and Hugging Face LeRobot](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/strands-physical-ai/index.md): Learn how to build physical AI systems that combine edge computing with cloud intelligence using Strands Agents, NVIDIA GR00T, and Hugging Face LeRobot.
- [Introducing Strands Agent SOPs – Natural Language Workflows for AI Agents](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/introducing-strands-agent-sops/index.md): Agent SOPs are a standardized markdown format for defining AI agent workflows in natural language that balances flexibility and control.
- [Strands Agents and the Model-Driven Approach](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/strands-agents-model-driven-approach/index.md): Learn how the model-driven approach in Strands Agents SDK lets modern LLMs drive their own behavior, making agents more resilient and adaptable.
- [Introducing Strands Agents 1.0: Production-Ready Multi-Agent Orchestration Made Simple](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/strands-agents-1-0/index.md): Strands Agents 1.0 brings multi-agent patterns, A2A protocol support, and production-ready features to the open source SDK.
- [Using Strands Agents with Claude 4 Interleaved Thinking](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/interleaved-thinking-claude-4/index.md): Learn how to use Claude 4's interleaved thinking beta feature with Strands Agents for faster, more fluid reasoning and reduced tool calls.
- [Introducing Strands Agents, an Open Source AI Agents SDK](http://github.programdotrun.com/harness-sdk/pr-cms-48/blog/introducing-strands-agents/index.md): Strands Agents is an open source SDK that takes a model-driven approach to building and running AI agents in just a few lines of code.
